# Nutrition Plan for Marathon Training

## Daily Caloric Target
**~2,800-3,200 calories/day** (adjust based on training intensity)

---

## Macronutrient Breakdown

| Nutrient | Amount | Purpose |
|----------|--------|---------|
| **Carbohydrates** | 55-65% (385-520g) | Fuel for long runs & glycogen stores |
| **Protein** | 15-20% (105-160g) | Muscle recovery & repair |
| **Fat** | 20-25% (62-89g) | Energy & hormone production |

---

## Sample Daily Eating Structure

### Breakfast
- Oatmeal with banana, berries, and honey
- Whole grain toast with almond butter
- Coffee or tea

### Mid-Morning Snack
- Greek yogurt with granola
- Or energy bar + fruit

### Lunch
- Grilled chicken or lean beef (150g)
- Brown rice or pasta (150g cooked)
- Vegetables (broccoli, carrots)
- Olive oil dressing

### Pre-Run Snack (2-3 hrs before)
- Banana with peanut butter
- Or rice cakes with jam

### Post-Run (Within 30 mins)
- Protein shake with berries
- Or chocolate milk + bagel

### Dinner
- Salmon or chicken (150g)
- Sweet potato (150g)
- Leafy greens with olive oil

### Evening Snack
- Cottage cheese with fruit
- Or nuts + dried fruit

---

## Carb-Loading Strategy (3 days before race)
- Increase carbs to 70-80% of calories
- Reduce fiber slightly to minimize GI issues
- Stay hydrated

**Hydration:** 3-4 liters water daily; electrolytes during long runs (>90 min)

## Daily Calorie & Macro Targets

**Estimated Daily Needs: 2,800–3,200 calories**
- **Protein: 164–180g** (2g per kg bodyweight)
- **Carbs: 350–420g** (4.3–5.1g per kg)
- **Fat: 93–107g** (1.1–1.3g per kg)

---

## Meal Structure

### Breakfast (600–700 cal)
- 3 whole eggs + 2 egg whites
- 80g oats with berries
- 1 tbsp almond butter

### Mid-Morning Snack (250–300 cal)
- Greek yogurt (200g) + granola + honey
- Or protein shake + banana

### Lunch (700–800 cal)
- 200g lean protein (chicken, beef, or fish)
- 200g rice or sweet potato
- Vegetables with olive oil

### Pre-Workout (200–250 cal) — *30–60 min before*
- 50g fast carbs (white rice, banana, honey)
- 20–25g protein (shake or chicken)

### Post-Workout (300–400 cal) — *Within 1–2 hours*
- 40–50g fast carbs (rice cakes, dextrose, juice)
- 30–40g protein (whey shake ideal)

### Dinner (700–800 cal)
- 200g protein + carbs + vegetables

### Evening (optional, 150–200 cal)
- Casein shake or cottage cheese

---

## Priority Foods

**Proteins:** Chicken, beef, fish, eggs, Greek yogurt, cottage cheese, whey

**Carbs:** Rice, oats, sweet potatoes, whole wheat pasta, fruits

**Fats:** Olive oil, nuts, avocado, fatty fish

**Hydration:** 3–4L water daily + electrolytes around training

---

## Post-Workout Optimization
✓ Fast carbs + protein within 1–2 hours
✓ Prioritize sleep (7–9 hours)
✓ Stay hydrated
✓ Creatine monohydrate (5g daily) — evidence-based

# Nutrition Plan for High-Intensity Swimming Training

## Daily Calorie Target
**~3,200-3,500 calories** (accounts for 2 daily training sessions + recovery needs)

---

## Pre-Workout Meals (1-2 hours before)

**Morning session:**
- Banana + almond butter + white toast
- Rice cakes with honey and jam
- Smoothie: banana, rice milk, maple syrup, rice protein powder

**Evening session:**
- White pasta with olive oil + salt
- White rice + grilled chicken breast
- Sweet potato + lean ground turkey

---

## Post-Workout Recovery (Within 30-45 min)

- **Protein + fast carbs** (critical for 2x daily training)
  - Chocolate rice milk shake + rice protein powder
  - White bagel + turkey
  - Rice with grilled salmon
  - Sweet potato + lean beef

---

## Main Meals

**Protein sources:** Chicken, turkey, salmon, white fish, lean beef, eggs

**Carbs:** White rice, white pasta, white bread, sweet potatoes, white potatoes, honey

**Fats:** Olive oil, avocado, nuts (almond, macadamia), fish oils

**Example:** Grilled salmon + white rice + olive oil drizzle

---

## Hydration & Electrolytes
- 3-4L water daily
- Electrolyte drink during/after swimming (sodium + potassium)
- Coconut water between sessions

---

## Foods to Avoid
❌ Dairy, high-fiber foods, fried foods, excessive fat, heavy meals before training
